categories.note: Auth boundaries, login/token behavior, SQL/NoSQL auth-bypass signals and rate behavior are tested when discoverable. Password-reset/MFA/business workflows still need configuration.
Same-role read-only path/query IDOR/BOLA is verified with test accounts. Complex workflow and state-changing authorization remain configuration-driven.
Cookie attributes and authenticated cache behavior are tested. Login-time rotation/fixation and logout invalidation require explicit disposable workflow configuration.
Database-error behavior plus SQL/NoSQL login-bypass proofs are tested when relevant endpoints are discovered; this is not exhaustive SQLi coverage.
Reflected and DOM execution can be verified with Playwright; stored XSS requires a configured write/read workflow.
Cookie/header auth posture and token signals are mapped. State-changing proof requires an explicitly configured disposable action.
URL-like GET parameters are tested only against a scanner-owned 127.0.0.1 callback. Cloud metadata/private services are not probed.
Upload security needs a disposable workflow definition so files can be safely created, retrieved, and removed.
Traversal candidates use known non-secret marker files; public backup/config/deployment artifacts are also signature-probed.
Endpoints and mixed ws:// usage are discovered. Full origin/auth handshake and message authorization testing needs a realtime workflow pack.
Requires explicit user journeys, invariants, and disposable test data.
Requires sandbox payment flows and business invariants.
Covers unauthenticated JSON, source maps, client artifacts, debug/status endpoints, backup archives, config files, heapdump exposure and sensitive URL parameters.
Covers DOM XSS signals, storage keys, postMessage, client redirects, mixed content, sensitive URLs, source maps and WebSocket discovery.
Needs configured password-reset/MFA/session-rotation workflows to prove takeover paths safely.
robots.txt/sitemap.xml and discovered routes can reveal hidden admin surfaces, but admin authorization workflows are not assumed.
Covers sensitive JSON fields, sensitive URL/query exposure, GET-form leakage and authenticated cross-account reads.
Covers headers, CORS, debug/status endpoints, source-control metadata, dependency manifests, backups and management endpoints.

protocol_security.detail: allowed methods: GET, OPTIONS, POST, TRACE

findings.title: Environment file is publicly exposed
findings.description: A publicly reachable .env response was confirmed.
findings.evidence: Environment-style secret keys were exposed: API_KEY, DATABASE_URL. Values were redacted.
findings.remediation: Block access immediately and rotate every credential that may have been exposed.

findings.title: NoSQL operator authentication bypass verified
findings.description: Synthetic NoSQL operator objects changed an invalid-login baseline into an authenticated success signal.
findings.evidence: The baseline invalid login was not successful; the $ne probe returned 2xx plus a session/token signal. No real credentials were used.
findings.remediation: Enforce scalar credential schemas and never pass untrusted query objects/operators into database credential lookups.

findings.title: SQL-style authentication bypass verified
findings.description: Synthetic SQL-style credentials changed an invalid-login baseline into an authenticated success signal.
findings.evidence: The baseline invalid login was not successful; the SQL-style probe returned 2xx plus a session/token signal. No real credentials were used.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized credential lookups and enforce strict scalar input schemas.

findings.title: Arbitrary CORS origin accepted with credentials
findings.description: The server reflected an untrusted Origin and explicitly allows credentials.
findings.evidence: Request Origin 'https://magic-security.invalid' was reflected as Access-Control-Allow-Origin. Access-Control-Allow-Credentials=true.
findings.remediation: Use an explicit allowlist of trusted origins and only enable credentials where required.

findings.title: Arbitrary CORS origin accepted with credentials
findings.description: The server reflected an untrusted Origin and explicitly allows credentials.
findings.evidence: Request Origin 'https://magic-security.invalid' was reflected as Access-Control-Allow-Origin. Access-Control-Allow-Credentials=true.
findings.remediation: Use an explicit allowlist of trusted origins and only enable credentials where required.

findings.title: CORS accepts null Origin with credentials
findings.description: The endpoint explicitly allows the null Origin used by sandboxed/file-like browser contexts.
findings.evidence: Origin: null was returned in Access-Control-Allow-Origin; credentials=true.
findings.remediation: Do not allow the null Origin unless a specific, reviewed use case requires it.

findings.title: Client artifact exposes secret-like material
findings.description: A browser-downloadable JavaScript/source-map artifact contains secret-like assignments or credential token shapes.
findings.evidence: Detected secret-like identifiers/types: API_SECRET. Values were intentionally redacted and not stored.
findings.remediation: Remove server credentials from frontend bundles/source maps and rotate any real secret that has already been published.

findings.title: Credentialed CORS policy exposes a protected endpoint
findings.description: A protected authenticated endpoint reflected an untrusted Origin and enabled credentials.
findings.evidence: Context 'user_a' received HTTP 200 while Origin 'https://magic-security.invalid' was reflected and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials was true. Response body and credential values were not stored.
findings.remediation: Use an explicit trusted-origin allowlist and never reflect arbitrary origins on credentialed protected endpoints.

findings.title: Cross-account object access verified (path)
findings.description: Authenticated same-role test contexts verified cross-account read access through path parameter 'account_id'.
findings.evidence: 'user_b' retrieved an object belonging to 'user_a' through a path parameter 'account_id'. Owner and cross-account responses were HTTP 200 and identical JSON. Credentials and raw object identifiers were not stored.
findings.remediation: Enforce object-level authorization for every request. Resolve requested resources through the authenticated principal's allowed scope rather than trusting client IDs.

findings.title: Cross-account object access verified (query)
findings.description: Authenticated same-role test contexts verified cross-account read access through query parameter 'account_id'.
findings.evidence: 'user_b' retrieved an object belonging to 'user_a' through a query parameter 'account_id'. Owner and cross-account responses were HTTP 200 and identical JSON. Credentials and raw object identifiers were not stored.
findings.remediation: Enforce object-level authorization for every request. Resolve requested resources through the authenticated principal's allowed scope rather than trusting client IDs.

findings.title: Git metadata is publicly exposed
findings.description: The repository HEAD file is reachable over HTTP.
findings.evidence: Server returned a Git HEAD reference: 'ref: refs/heads/main'.
findings.remediation: Block access to .git and review whether repository history exposed credentials or sensitive files.

findings.title: HTTP response header injection verified
findings.description: A query parameter injected a new HTTP response header.
findings.evidence: Parameter 'value' caused the inert scanner header X-Magic-Security-Probe: verified to appear in the response.
findings.remediation: Reject CR/LF characters in header-derived input and use framework header APIs that prevent response splitting.

findings.title: HTTP response header injection verified
findings.description: A query parameter injected a new HTTP response header.
findings.evidence: Parameter 'next' caused the inert scanner header X-Magic-Security-Probe: verified to appear in the response.
findings.remediation: Reject CR/LF characters in header-derived input and use framework header APIs that prevent response splitting.

findings.title: HTTP response header injection verified
findings.description: A query parameter injected a new HTTP response header.
findings.evidence: Parameter 'name' caused the inert scanner header X-Magic-Security-Probe: verified to appear in the response.
findings.remediation: Reject CR/LF characters in header-derived input and use framework header APIs that prevent response splitting.

findings.title: Path traversal / local file read verified
findings.description: Parameter 'file' allowed a traversal sequence to read a known operating-system marker file.
findings.evidence: The response matched the non-secret marker set 'unix_hosts'. File contents were not stored.
findings.remediation: Resolve files from a fixed allowlisted root, reject traversal segments, and avoid accepting raw filesystem paths.

findings.title: Public configuration exposes secret-like keys
findings.description: A public JSON configuration/debug endpoint revealed environment or secret-like key names.
findings.evidence: Detected secret-like key names: api_key. Values were not stored.
findings.remediation: Restrict the endpoint and rotate any credential that may have been publicly exposed.

findings.title: Reflected XSS execution verified
findings.description: A controlled reflected value executed JavaScript in the target browser origin.
findings.evidence: Parameter 'q' executed a non-network DOM-only canary in a headless browser. No cookies, storage values, or external callbacks were read.
findings.remediation: Use context-aware output encoding, remove unsafe raw HTML rendering, and deploy a restrictive CSP as defense in depth.

findings.title: Secret/authentication material appears in URL
findings.description: Parameter 'token' was observed with a value in a URL. URLs can leak through browser history, logs, analytics, screenshots, and referrers.
findings.evidence: Observed populated URL parameter name: token. The parameter value was not stored.
findings.remediation: Move sensitive values to request bodies or secure cookies/headers and avoid placing credentials or PII in URLs.

findings.title: Sensitive form fields are submitted with GET
findings.description: A discovered GET form contains credential, token, personal, or payment-like field names.
findings.evidence: Sensitive field names: password. Values were not captured.
findings.remediation: Submit sensitive forms with POST over HTTPS and keep secret values out of query strings.

findings.title: Server-side request forgery verified
findings.description: Parameter 'url' caused the target server to request a scanner-owned loopback callback.
findings.evidence: A unique callback token was received by the local scanner callback server. No external host or metadata endpoint was contacted.
findings.remediation: Allowlist outbound destinations and block loopback/private/link-local targets after DNS resolution and redirect handling.

findings.title: Server-side template injection verified
findings.description: A harmless arithmetic template expression was evaluated server-side and its computed result appeared in the response.
findings.evidence: Parameter 'name' evaluated the scanner's arithmetic-only template canary. No file, process, network, or environment access was attempted.
findings.remediation: Never render untrusted input as a template. Pass user values as data and use sandboxed template configuration where available.

findings.title: Server-side template injection verified
findings.description: A harmless arithmetic template expression was evaluated server-side and its computed result appeared in the response.
findings.evidence: Parameter 'name' evaluated the scanner's arithmetic-only template canary. No file, process, network, or environment access was attempted.
findings.remediation: Never render untrusted input as a template. Pass user values as data and use sandboxed template configuration where available.

findings.title: User-specific authenticated response is marked for shared caching
findings.description: A protected response that differs between users is explicitly cacheable by shared caches.
findings.evidence: Context 'user_a' received HTTP 200 with Cache-Control='public, max-age=120'. The authenticated response body was not stored.
findings.remediation: Use Cache-Control: private or no-store for user-specific authenticated responses and review CDN/proxy cache rules.

findings.title: Debug or stack-trace information exposed
findings.description: The response appears to contain framework or exception debug output.
findings.evidence: Matched debug signature: 'Traceback (most recent call last)'.
findings.remediation: Disable debug output in production and return generic error responses.

findings.title: Input triggers a database error response
findings.description: A controlled query mutation caused a database-specific error signature that was absent from the baseline.
findings.evidence: Parameter 'q' triggered a database error signature after an apostrophe probe. The response body and database details were not retained.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries and generic production error handling. Review this endpoint manually for SQL injection.

findings.title: JSONP-style arbitrary callback wrapping verified
findings.description: A caller-controlled callback name was used to wrap the endpoint response as executable JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Parameter 'callback' accepted the scanner callback identifier. Response data was not stored and no script was executed.
findings.remediation: Prefer CORS-protected JSON APIs instead of JSONP, especially for authenticated or sensitive data.

findings.title: Open redirect verified
findings.description: The 'next' parameter can redirect a visitor to an arbitrary external origin.
findings.evidence: A controlled request set 'next' to 'https://magic-security.invalid/verified-redirect'; the server returned HTTP 302 with Location='https://magic-security.invalid/verified-redirect'.
findings.remediation: Allow only relative paths or validate redirect destinations against an explicit allowlist.

findings.title: Open redirect verified
findings.description: The 'next' parameter can redirect a visitor to an arbitrary external origin.
findings.evidence: A controlled request set 'next' to 'https://magic-security.invalid/verified-redirect'; the server returned HTTP 302 with Location='https://magic-security.invalid/verified-redirect'.
findings.remediation: Allow only relative paths or validate redirect destinations against an explicit allowlist.

findings.title: Reflected HTML injection verified
findings.description: A controlled query value was inserted into returned HTML as markup instead of being safely encoded.
findings.evidence: Parameter 'name' created the scanner's inert custom HTML element in the parsed response. The random canary value was not retained.
findings.remediation: Apply context-aware output encoding and avoid inserting untrusted values with raw HTML rendering APIs.

findings.title: Reflected HTML injection verified
findings.description: A controlled query value was inserted into returned HTML as markup instead of being safely encoded.
findings.evidence: Parameter 'name' created the scanner's inert custom HTML element in the parsed response. The random canary value was not retained.
findings.remediation: Apply context-aware output encoding and avoid inserting untrusted values with raw HTML rendering APIs.

findings.title: Unauthenticated JSON exposes sensitive-looking fields
findings.description: A GET request with no authentication or session cookies returned HTTP 200 JSON containing these security-relevant field names: email, phone.
findings.evidence: Unauthenticated HTTP 200 JSON contained field paths: users.email, users.phone. Values were intentionally not stored.
findings.remediation: Confirm the data is intended to be public. If not, require authentication and enforce object/field-level authorization.

findings.title: Untrusted Host header influences response content
findings.description: A scanner-controlled Host/X-Forwarded-Host value was incorporated into response content or Location.
findings.evidence: The marker host appeared only in the poisoned-host response. No password-reset poisoning was claimed.
findings.remediation: Validate Host against an explicit allowlist and configure trusted proxy host handling correctly.

findings.title: Client artifact reveals internal network locations
findings.description: A browser-downloadable artifact references private/internal network URLs.
findings.evidence: Detected 1 unique private/internal URL reference(s); values were not listed.
findings.remediation: Remove unnecessary internal topology references from production client artifacts.

findings.title: Cookie session is missing security attributes
findings.description: The cookie is missing: HttpOnly, SameSite.
findings.evidence: Set-Cookie for session lacked HttpOnly, SameSite. Cookie value is intentionally redacted.
findings.remediation: Add the appropriate Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite attributes based on the cookie purpose.

findings.title: Frontend source map is publicly exposed
findings.description: A valid JavaScript source map is publicly downloadable.
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 returned a valid source map referencing 1 source file(s). Embedded source content: yes.
findings.remediation: Disable production source-map publication unless it is intentionally required.

findings.title: HTTP TRACE method reflects request data
findings.description: The server accepted TRACE and reflected a controlled request header.
findings.evidence: TRACE returned the scanner's inert marker. No credentials or browser data were sent.
findings.remediation: Disable TRACE unless it is explicitly required.

findings.title: Page lacks clickjacking frame protection
findings.description: The HTML response has no observed anti-framing policy.
findings.evidence: Neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors was present.
findings.remediation: Set CSP frame-ancestors to the intended embedding policy and optionally X-Frame-Options for legacy clients.

findings.title: Potential DOM XSS source-to-sink path
findings.description: Browser-controlled input sources and unsafe DOM sinks coexist in a client artifact.
findings.evidence: frontend JavaScript contains browser-controlled source(s) location.search, location.hash and unsafe DOM sink(s) innerHTML.
findings.remediation: Trace the data flow and replace unsafe sinks or apply context-appropriate sanitization.

findings.title: Potential client-side redirect flow
findings.description: Client code combines browser-controlled URL input with client-side navigation sinks.
findings.evidence: frontend JavaScript combines URL source(s) location.search, location.hash with navigation sink(s) location.href.
findings.remediation: Restrict client-side redirect destinations to safe relative paths or an explicit allowlist.

findings.title: Potentially dangerous HTTP methods advertised
findings.description: The server advertises HTTP methods that are rarely required for ordinary web applications.
findings.evidence: OPTIONS advertised: TRACE
findings.remediation: Restrict allowed HTTP methods at the application and proxy layers.

findings.title: Sensitive-looking browser storage key observed
findings.description: A JavaScript-accessible browser storage entry has a security-relevant key name.
findings.evidence: localStorage contains security-relevant key 'access_token'. The stored value was not read or recorded.
findings.remediation: Avoid keeping bearer credentials or sensitive session material in localStorage/sessionStorage when a safer server-side or HttpOnly-cookie design is available.

findings.title: Session-like cookie demo_session lacks protective attributes
findings.description: An authenticated response set a session-like cookie without all expected browser-side protections.
findings.evidence: Cookie 'demo_session' was observed for context 'user_a'; missing: HttpOnly, SameSite. The cookie value was not stored.
findings.remediation: Use HttpOnly for session cookies, set an explicit SameSite policy, and use Secure whenever the cookie is transported over HTTPS.

findings.title: Web message handler lacks an obvious origin check
findings.description: Frontend code registers a cross-window message handler without an obvious origin-validation signal.
findings.evidence: A message event handler was found; no obvious event.origin validation signal was found.
findings.remediation: Validate event.origin against a strict trusted-origin allowlist before processing message data.

findings.title: API documentation is publicly exposed
findings.description: Swagger/OpenAPI documentation appears reachable from the scanned surface.
findings.evidence: The page path and response content both contain API documentation markers.
findings.remediation: Keep public API docs only if intentional; otherwise restrict access in production.

findings.title: Anonymous GraphQL introspection is enabled
findings.description: The GraphQL schema can be introspected without authentication.
findings.evidence: A minimal introspection query returned __schema metadata with HTTP 200.
findings.remediation: Keep introspection public only when intentional. Otherwise restrict it in production while preserving schema access for trusted tooling.

findings.title: Missing content-security-policy
findings.description: Content-Security-Policy is not configured.
findings.evidence: Response did not contain the content-security-policy header.
findings.remediation: Add a restrictive CSP appropriate for the application.

findings.title: Missing referrer-policy
findings.description: Referrer-Policy is not configured.
findings.evidence: Response did not contain the referrer-policy header.
findings.remediation: Set an explicit Referrer-Policy suitable for the application.

findings.title: Missing x-content-type-options
findings.description: X-Content-Type-Options is not configured.
findings.evidence: Response did not contain the x-content-type-options header.
findings.remediation: Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

findings.title: OpenAPI specification is publicly exposed
findings.description: A machine-readable API specification is publicly reachable.
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 returned JSON containing openapi metadata.
findings.remediation: Keep it public only if intentional; otherwise restrict production access.

findings.title: Server reveals server technology
findings.description: The response exposes server/framework fingerprint information.
findings.evidence: Server header was present. The exact value is omitted.
findings.remediation: Remove unnecessary version/product disclosure where practical.
